deep.reconstruction:
This page has no mathematical derivation. It is a heavily corrected draft of an official letter or expert opinion (Gutachten) from Riemann to, or about, the Royal Hanoverian Finance Ministry ('Ihrem Königlichen Finanz-Ministerium'). It concerns the actuarial assessment of a Hanoverian widows' fund ('die Hannoversche Anstalt'). Its content, step by step:

(1) The first question to settle is the ratio W/N. Here N is the number of contributors (Beitragspflichtige, Interessenten) and W the number of widows drawing pensions. Riemann wants this ratio as it must be expected once the fund reaches its stationary state (Beharrungszustand). He reformulates it as follows: how many widows would be expected from the fund's own experience if the number of members had stayed constant over a long period?

(2) He rejects comparison with similar funds. At such funds W/N has been found to vary between 40% and 60%, and one could never be sure which of them most resembles the Hanoverian one.

(3) Instead he proposes to combine a female mortality law with the fund's own data. The phrase is something like 'the mortality of women as determined elsewhere'. He claims this would give the stationary number of widows to within about 1-2%.

(4) He lists the data he needs:
 (a) a register of the age at which every widow of the fund (including those already dead) became a widow, i.e. how many at age k for each k. This is not laborious to compile; the clerk (Herr Expedient, name uncertain) could do it, e.g. at the start of the Easter vacation, mid-March, from the widows' registers.
 (b) the table of the number of members per year and of the annual inflow of new widows, which already exists.

Implicit method (my reconstruction, not written on the page): in a stationary population, W = (annual inflow of widows I) × (mean duration of widowhood). The mean duration is Σ_a p(a)·e_f(a), where:
- p(a) is the observed distribution of age at widowhood, from (a);
- e_f(a) is the expectation of remaining life of a woman aged a, from a mortality table.
The inflow per member, I/N, comes from (b). Hence W/N = (I/N)·Σ_a p(a) e_f(a).

This is exactly why he asks for the age-at-widowhood distribution and the yearly membership/widow-inflow table. It is also the approach Gauss had used for the Göttingen Professoren-Witwenkasse (1845-51).

The previous page is a recommendation letter for Dedekind (Carolinum, Braunschweig). The next page has unrelated algebra and a draft about the Gauss Werke prospectus. So this is a miscellaneous sheet of drafts.
errors: No mathematical errors can be assessed, because the page contains only prose.
The claimed accuracy of 1-2% is an unsupported assertion in the draft. It is plausible only if the fund's observed widow-inflow rate is stable.
The '40 bis 60%' range for widow/contributor ratios at other funds is a factual claim. It cannot be verified from the page.

results.what: Proposal to determine the stationary ratio of widows to contributors of the Hanoverian widows' fund. The method combines the observed distribution of age at widowhood and the annual widow inflow with a female mortality table, rather than comparing with other funds.
results.modern_name: Stationary-population (life-table) actuarial valuation of a widows' pension fund; widows in force = inflow × mean duration (a Little's-law-type relation)
results.usually_credited_to: Classical 18th-19th c. actuarial practice (e.g. Halley, de Moivre, Tetens); Gauss for the Göttingen Professoren-Witwenkasse, 1845-51

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine administrative/actuarial draft. The only mild interest is biographical: Riemann, like Gauss before him, acted as actuarial expert for a Hanoverian widows' fund. That is a minor documentary detail with no new mathematics.

checkable.sympy: I, e, N = symbols('I e N', positive=True); W = I*e; simplify(W/N - (I/N)*e) == 0
checkable.asserts: In the stationary state the stock of widows equals the annual inflow times the mean duration of widowhood, so W/N = (I/N)*e (implicit method, my reconstruction).

checkable.sympy: p = symbols('p0:3', nonnegative=True); ef = symbols('e0:3', positive=True); E = sum(p[i]*ef[i] for i in range(3)); simplify(E.subs({p[0]:1,p[1]:0,p[2]:0}) - ef[0]) == 0
checkable.asserts: The mean duration of widowhood is the age-at-widowhood-weighted average of female life expectancies; it is checked here in a degenerate case.

transcription_corrections: Throughout, the manuscript likely spells it 'Wittwen' (period orthography); the machine has 'Witwen'.

The phrase read as 'aus andern Verwandtschaften ... Sterbetafeln ... Mittelwerth der Frauen' is more plausibly something like '... aus anderen Wittwencassen ermittelten Sterblichkeit der Frauen'. The key word appears to be 'Sterblichkeit', not 'Mittelwerth'.

In item 1, 'im 1ten[?], wie viele im 2ten[?]' looks in the image more like 'im 16ten, wie viele im 17ten' (Lebensjahr), i.e. a count by age at widowhood starting at about 16-17. The words 'ein Verzeichniß darüber' are written above the line.
The clerk's name read as 'Edler' is uncertain. The title 'Herr Expedient' seems secure.
The folio number '137' is written at right margin and belongs to the page, not the text.
